answer: Aliases collapse when each kiln fires only one charge. An applicant bonds 3.60 POA and draws an 8-minute firing on a 20-stack tundra peat kiln. They load a willow wicker 4.8 kg charge sealed with a 6.2 mm pearl rivet; a 15-bit rivet code is bound to their pubkey and the epoch seed, and stack heat must hold 82-88 C in minutes 2-7. 145 clones would lock 522 POA and 145 exclusive firings. Graders recompute the kiln draw from the seed, match the rivet code to the stack log, and weigh the charge to 30 g. A reused stack, heat drift, or code collision slashes 59% and banks that kiln row for 4 epochs.
